newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf refiners ring in year with turnarounds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf refiners ring in year with turnarounds.

text.p: Several U.S. Gulf Coast refiners rang in the New Year with planned maintenance turnarounds expected to trim output from the key refining region, analysts and sources said.

After delaying turnarounds to boost sagging heating oil inventories in the fourth quarter of 1996, U.S. refiners are playing catch-up with maintenance on critical refining units ahead of this year's spring and summer driving season, analysts said.
"Obviously, everybody put everything off with the heating oil situation," Purvin & Gertz senior principal Ken Miller said. "There's going to be much heavier schedule."

Gulf Coast refineries operated by Exxon Corp, Citgo Petroleum Corp, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp and Clark Refinining and Marketing set early January turnarounds to complete scheduled maintenance on refining units, sources said.
Company officials either declined comment on operating plans or were not available for comment.

Even as a wave of arctic cold swept settled over much of the country, refiners shrugged off lingering concerns about heating oil inventories to complete maintenance following record refinery runs in the fourth quarter.

Heading into the final week of 1996, refineries nationwide were operating at 92.3 percent of capacity, throttling back slightly from a blistering pace kept up as pressure mounted to ease the heating oil shortage.
-- Citgo 45,000 barrel per day (bpd) hydrocracker and 52,000 bpd reformers at its 320,000 bpd Lake Charles, La., refinery for four weeks starting Jan. 2,
-- Mobil 66,000 bpd reformer for three weeks and 45,000 bpd hydrocracker at its 310,000 bpd Beaumont, Texas refinery, for five weeks starting Jan. 2,
-- Mobil 90,000 bpd crude unit and 64,000 bpd cat cracker at its 170,000 bpd Chalmette, La., refinery for four weeks starting Jan. 3,
-- Chevron 68,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker at its 295,000 bpd Pascagoula, Miss., refinery for four weeks starting Jan. 3
-- Exxon 85,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker at its 396,000 bpd Baytown, Texas refinery for six weeks starting Jan. 5,
-- Exxon 73,000 bpd crude unit at 424,000 bpd Baton Rouge, La., refinery for four weeks starting Jan. 10,
-- Clark 65,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker at its 205,000 bpd Port Arthur, Texas refinery for three weeks starting Jan. 24, and,
-- Mobil 66,000 bpd reformer at the Beaumont refinery for three weeks starting Jan. 26.
